module_title: Non-Constitutional Bodies - NITI Aayog, NHRC & CBI (Basics)
introduction: Non-Constitutional bodies are those not mentioned in the original Constitution of India but created by an Act of Parliament (Statutory) or an Executive Order. This level covers the basic identity and establishment of India's premier think tank, rights watchdog, and premier investigating agency.

core_concepts.title: NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India)
core_concepts.description: Established on January 1, 2015, via an executive resolution to replace the 65-year-old Planning Commission. It serves as the 'Think Tank' of the Government of India.

core_concepts.title: National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)
core_concepts.description: A statutory body established in 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act. Its purpose is to protect and promote human rights relating to life, liberty, equality, and dignity.

core_concepts.title: Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)
core_concepts.description: Established in 1963 by a resolution of the Ministry of Home Affairs. It is the main investigating agency of the Central Government for corruption and major crimes.

core_concepts.title: Executive vs. Statutory Bodies
core_concepts.description: NITI Aayog and CBI are Executive bodies (created by government order), whereas NHRC is a Statutory body (created by a law passed by Parliament).

important_entities.name: Chairperson of NITI Aayog
important_entities.significance: Ensures the body has the highest political authority to coordinate between states and center.

important_entities.name: NHRC Chairperson
important_entities.key_fact: Retired Chief Justice of India or a Judge of the Supreme Court
important_entities.significance: Ensures judicial expertise in handling human rights violations.

important_entities.name: Director of CBI
important_entities.key_fact: IG of Police, Delhi Special Police Establishment
important_entities.significance: Responsible for the administration of the agency.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: CBI is NOT a Statutory Body
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A common mistake is thinking CBI was created by a law. It actually derives its powers from the 'Delhi Special Police Establishment (DSPE) Act, 1946', but it wasn't created by it.
Unlike the Finance Commission (Art. 280), NITI Aayog has no article in the Constitution.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Many exams swap 'Institution' for 'Institute'. Remember: National **Institution** for Transforming India.
NHRC (1993) and NITI (2015) are the most frequently asked dates.

exam_strategy_tips: Always differentiate between bodies created by 'Act' (Statutory) and 'Order' (Executive).
Identify the 'Think Tank' keyword for NITI Aayog.
